normal:
Use case: identity-preserve. Asset type: production game character animation spritesheet. Input image is the approved character identity and art style reference. Produce ONE character only: the ordinary GREEN zombie at top middle-right of reference: lime-green skin, turquoise spiky mohawk, pink headband, huge yellow eyes, open silly mouth/tongue, torn sleeveless blue denim vest, brown ragged shorts, small black shoes. Preserve that character's clothing, facial features, colors and equipment exactly. Bright polished hand-painted cartoon 2D game sprites with dark readable outlines, slightly elevated FRONT camera looking down, character faces screen-bottom, same scale and camera in every frame. Actual transparent background, no ground shadow, no scenery, no labels, no effects, no grid lines.
Exactly 8 separate full-body poses in a strict 4-column 2-row sprite sheet. Equal-size spacious cells with transparent gutters; each character fits entirely in its own cell. 1536 x 1024 canvas, same character scale, both feet visible, pelvis centered in each cell, feet at consistent ground baseline. Do not resize each pose individually.
ROW ONE: four genuinely different alternating walking poses. Frame 0 left foot forward planted, right foot back raised. Frame 1 left support with right knee lifted passing forward. Frame 2 right foot forward planted, left foot back raised. Frame 3 right support with left knee lifted passing forward. Strongly visible alternating legs and counter swinging arms. Keep direction facing down screen. Not a shifted or rotated duplicate.
ROW TWO: four standing hit-reaction poses. Feet shoulder-width apart planted in exactly identical positions and pelvis aligned across all four. Frame 4 prepared stance, elbows slightly bent. Frame 5 impact: upper torso and head visibly recoil backward, chin lifts, arms recoil up/out, feet stay planted. Frame 6 recovery: torso leans forward back toward prepared stance and arms lower. Frame 7 neutral recovered stance. Keep thighs, knees, boots and pelvis same size and same position across row two. Hands should remain above or outside the waist seam so they can be preserved during fixed-lower-body compositing. NO blood, no deformation, no new items.
